Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

BlackThriveSS (development version)

  • Robustness analysis. btg_sensitivity() bounds every ratio under the two extreme allocations of stops with no recorded ethnicity and reports parity_direction and the best and worst rank each force could hold; btg_rank_stability() gives seeded rank intervals and top-n probabilities from Poisson redraws of the recorded counts, leaving the caller’s random number state untouched; btg_plot_sensitivity() draws the ranking chart’s forces with their sampling interval and allocation range on a log axis. Sampling variability and assumption ranges are never combined.
  • Time. btg_plot_trend() draws a force’s or council’s ratios or rates over the years, national monthly stops or shares, national totals and rates, outcome-linked search rates and Section 60 searches, with incomplete periods marked and never annualised; btg_change() compares two years with an interval and the coverage of both; btg_plot_change() is a dumbbell chart of the largest changes. btg_group_colours() gives every group a fixed colour.
  • Briefings. btg_profile() gathers the evidence for one force or council as plain statements that carry their qualifications, with the tables behind them; btg_report() renders a self-contained HTML briefing from the installed R Markdown template “BlackThriveSS briefing”, which the editors also list under new R Markdown templates, as a self-contained web page or a Word document.
  • Sharing. btg_export() writes a dataset to CSV with a JSON provenance sidecar; btg_glossary() defines every term the package uses.
  • Auditing the source. btg_source_status() reads the Police.uk availability feed and reports months published since the snapshot and any force-month inside the verified window that has been added or withdrawn; it is the package’s only use of the network and fails quietly with a message. btg_robustness_summary() gives one row per year and group with the counts a study of robustness starts from.
  • Saved views gain schema 3, which carries a dataset selection and a chart’s settings, so trend and change charts replay like the ranking charts; the sensitivity chart replays through schema 2. Earlier views are unchanged. The default year for comparisons is now the latest year the source covers in full for every dataset, including councils.
  • Two new vignettes, “How robust is a disparity estimate?” and “Brief a force or council”, and a pkgdown site configuration.
  • Help pages are now generated with roxygen2 8.1; the package help page lists the repository and issue tracker at https://github.com/BlackThrive/BlackThriveSS, which DESCRIPTION records.

BlackThriveSS 0.0.3

  • A dataset catalogue. A second immutable release adds six datasets built from the same dashboard snapshot: force_ethnicity_year (every year from 2018 and all four groups compared with White, reproducing the 2025 Black rows of force_disparity exactly), national_year, national_month_ethnicity, council_ethnicity_year, hit_rate_ethnicity_year and section60_force_year. btg_datasets() and btg_releases() describe them; btg_get_data() gains groups and council arguments and accepts several years; btg_validate() audits every dataset. The original 2025 release and its saved views are unchanged. Months outside the dashboard’s verification window are unverified, never assumed supplied.

  • A round trip with the dashboard website. btg_dashboard_url() turns a chart into the link that opens the Disparity page at the same year, group and selected force, in either link form the dashboard reads; btg_from_url() reproduces the chart behind a link copied from the website, warning when the link was made from a different source month. btg_dashboard_base() and the option BlackThriveSS.dashboard_url choose the deployment.

  • btg_plot_disparity() draws any year and group from force_ethnicity_year and can highlight one force as the dashboard’s selected force. Saved views move to schema 2 to carry the year, group and highlight; schema 1 files still replay.

  • Redrew the ranking chart with a shared visual system. New exported btg_theme() and btg_colours() carry the dashboard’s amber and navy into a quiet ggplot2 theme: hairline grid, titles aligned with the plot edge, thinner bars, a labelled parity line and finer axis breaks. Each bar now carries its 95% Poisson interval, forces with incomplete or unverified returns are drawn in a lighter fill with a legend as well as the asterisk, and the subtitle states how many of the eligible forces are shown. The evidence table and saved-view format are unchanged.

BlackThriveSS 0.0.2

  • Added a portable installation bundle with dependency resolution and archive checksums.
  • Added an installed, executable getting-started vignette and standard package citation.
  • Added btg_validate() for accounting, reporting-coverage and estimate consistency.
  • Added corrupt-data regression tests and source-checksum checks for dashboard parity.
  • Added a multi-platform CI configuration, release scripts and a CRAN readiness checklist.
  • Explicitly deferred the dashboard Use in R button.
  • Preserved the existing fixed dataset release and saved-view format.

BlackThriveSS 0.0.1

Initial development slice:

  • One offline, immutable 2025 force-disparity dataset derived from the local dashboard.
  • Black:White ranking chart returned as an editable ggplot, with chart data export.
  • Monthly submission coverage, original counts and populations, source checksums, explicit limitations and dataset citation.
  • Strict JSON saved views pin the release, selection, payload checksums and chart version.
  • Dashboard parity and independent known-answer validation.

This is a local development package, not a CRAN release or hosted data service.
